item.title: [Recap] Marcus Smart (HOU): Marcus Smart (suspension) finished Wednesday’s win over the Pacers with four points (1-of-4 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer.
item.description:
Marcus Smart (suspension) finished Wednesday’s win over the Pacers with four points (1-of-4 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer.

After serving a three-game suspension for throwing a punch at Warriors center Charles Bassey, Smart returned to the Rockets’ rotation on Wednesday. He took on his usual bench role, which offers little fantasy value when Fred VanVleet and Reed Sheppard are available. Fantasy managers can leave Smart on the waiver wire, as he’s scored in double figures twice in 10 games this season.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Jaxson Hayes (UTA): Jaxson Hayes (knee) finished Wednesday’s win over the Lakers with six points (2-of-5 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks.
item.description:
Jaxson Hayes (knee) finished Wednesday’s win over the Lakers with six points (2-of-5 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks.

Available after a two-game absence, Hayes came off the bench on Wednesday night. However, he still played more than starter Mo Bamba, who logged 22 minutes and finished with six points, 16 rebounds, one steal and two blocks. With that minutes split in Hayes’ first game back, it may not take him long to move into the starting lineup.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Walker Kessler (LAL): Walker Kessler had a stat line of 10 points (3-of-7 FGs, 4-of-10 FTs), 11 rebounds, and an assist against his former team, the Jazz on Wednesday.
item.description:
Walker Kessler had a stat line of 10 points (3-of-7 FGs, 4-of-10 FTs), 11 rebounds, and an assist against his former team, the Jazz on Wednesday.

Walker Kessler had a good performance except for the free throw percentage where he went 4-of-10. There might be a slight buy low opportunity here for Walker if someone is mad about the FT% and the lack of scoring that he’s had over the past few games. He should bounce back, but he’s not the player that people saw in the first two games of the season where he looked amazing.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Quentin Grimes (LAL): Quentin Grimes got 20 points (8-of-20 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, and four 3-pointers in loss on Wednesday to Jazz.
item.description:
Quentin Grimes got 20 points (8-of-20 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, and four 3-pointers in loss on Wednesday to Jazz.

Grimes continued his run after an insane game against the Hornets on Tuesday. He’s been the big beneficiary of the Reaves injury at this point. He’s wroth having until Reaves comes back, but once he does, he’s a streamer for points and 3’s only. The usage won’t be the same as it was during this run. This is a sell high if you have him on your roster currently.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Luka Dončić (LAL): Luka Dončić scored 29 points (10-of-28 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), got five rebounds, seven assists, two steals, two 3-pointers, and 9 turnovers in 109-97 loss to Jazz.
item.description:
Luka Dončić scored 29 points (10-of-28 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), got five rebounds, seven assists, two steals, two 3-pointers, and 9 turnovers in 109-97 loss to Jazz.

The run that Luka is on this season is incredible. You can pencil him in for a great game every night and there’s nothing the opponent can do about it. It wasn’t even the best night and he still produced. You wish the turnovers are lower, but he’s having to do everything for this team, especially with Austin Reaves out of the lineup.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Ace Bailey (UTA): Ace Bailey got himself 19 points (7-of-19 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, a steal, and two 3-pointers on Wednesday.
item.description:
Ace Bailey got himself 19 points (7-of-19 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, a steal, and two 3-pointers on Wednesday.

Ace has been more inconsistent as of late with his shooting, but the Jazz needed offense with Darryn being in foul trouble, and Ace at least put up shots and impacted the game in other ways defensively. There might be a bit of a buy low still with the efficiency, especially with the 3PT shooting being as low as it is, but he’s been great this year for the Jazz.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Svi Mykhailiuk (UTA): Svi Mykhailiuk put up 15 points (4-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and four 3-pointers in win on Wednesday.
item.description:
Svi Mykhailiuk put up 15 points (4-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and four 3-pointers in win on Wednesday.

It’s been a terrible start to the season for Svi. He wasn’t going to continue to shoot as poorly as he has, so it’s nice to see a decent bounce back game from him. He’s only a player for deeper leagues as a streamer, but it’s good to commend him for his performance tonight since he played 34 minutes with Darryn Peterson getting into foul trouble.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Keyonte George (UTA): Keyonte Geroge scores 30 points (9-of-17 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), a rebound, ten assists, a steal, and five 3-pointers in the 109-97 win over the Lakers.
item.description:
Keyonte Geroge scores 30 points (9-of-17 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), a rebound, ten assists, a steal, and five 3-pointers in the 109-97 win over the Lakers.

George was carrying the offense for the Jazz and keeping them in the first half of this game. Darryn Peterson was having foul trouble, so it was on him to keep the Jazz in the game. He helped lead them to get the win in this one. It’s been great back-to-back games for Keyonte and there might be a sell high window here.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Jayson Tatum (BOS): Jayson Tatum had 24 points (10-of-23 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers against the Nuggets on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jayson Tatum had 24 points (10-of-23 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers against the Nuggets on Wednesday.

Tatum led the Celtics with 24 points Wednesday, but a late technical foul proved costly in the loss to the Nuggets. The 28-year-old forward was assessed a technical foul in the final seconds of the game for throwing the ball in the direction of an official. This allowed Jamal Murray to make the technical free throw and ice the game for the Nuggets by extending the Denver lead to four. The Celtics begin a back-to-back against the Kings and Warriors on the road Saturday.

Nick Shlain

item.title: [Recap] Jamal Murray (DEN): Jamal Murray had 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals, two blocks and two three-pointers against the Celtics on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jamal Murray had 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals, two blocks and two three-pointers against the Celtics on Wednesday.

Murray was excellent and finished with a complete stat line against the Celtics Wednesday. The 29-year-old guard hit a clutch jumper to put the Nuggets up by three with less than 10 seconds left in regulation. Following a technical foul on Jayson Tatum, Murray then hit a free throw to ice the game. Denver improved to 8-5 on the season while the Celtics fell to 11-4.

Nick Shlain

item.title: [Recap] Domantas Sabonis (SAC): Domantas Sabonis accounted for eight points (4-of-7 FGs), 13 rebounds, eight assists and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Suns.
item.description:
Domantas Sabonis accounted for eight points (4-of-7 FGs), 13 rebounds, eight assists and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Suns.

Sabonis’ rebounding and assist numbers will certainly help fantasy managers. However, he attempted seven shots against the Suns, dropping his season average to 8.6 attempts per game. He’s struggled more than fellow veteran Zach LaVine to adjust to rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. However, Domas is still providing top-50 fantasy value because of what he’s done outside of scoring.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Zach LaVine (SAC): Zach LaVine tallied 18 points (8-of-12 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Suns.
item.description:
Zach LaVine tallied 18 points (8-of-12 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Suns.

LaVine returned to the Kings’ lineup on Wednesday after an illness kept him out of Sunday’s loss to the Thunder. While he shot the ball well, the veteran guard’s presence was enough to keep the Kings from finishing their home stand with a seventh straight loss. LaVine has been close to a top-50 player so far, outperforming his ADP.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Charles Bassey (GSW): Charles Bassey put up 10 points (5-of-8 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, a steal, a block, and four turnovers in loss.
item.description:
Charles Bassey put up 10 points (5-of-8 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, a steal, a block, and four turnovers in loss.

Bassey has been a great find for the Warriors this season. They’ve needed his rebounding and presence in the paint considering that they haven’t had Kristaps all season, and Horford is older. In redraft leagues, he’s primarily a streamer and not much more than that.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Yaxel Lendeborg (GSW): Yaxel Lendeborg gets 13 points (6-of-18 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, and two steals in the 116-94 loss to the Mavericks.
item.description:
Yaxel Lendeborg gets 13 points (6-of-18 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, and two steals in the 116-94 loss to the Mavericks.

For the numbers that Yaxel has been putting up since Steph has gone out, it wasn’t a great game. The Warriors as a team have really been missing Steph and his presence on the court. He’s been getting shots up which is great to see, but it hasn’t resulted in wins. In a redraft league, he’s been a great steal from where you got him.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Will Richard (GSW): Will Richards had himself a night with 20 points (9-of-13 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), three assists, four steals, and a three in the loss to the Mavericks.
item.description:
Will Richards had himself a night with 20 points (9-of-13 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), three assists, four steals, and a three in the loss to the Mavericks.

Will was the only players on the Warriors that could get his offense consistently in this game. It’s honestly impressive considering he’s playing with his thumb wrapped up and he was hitting shots in this one. Getting the four steals is a nice bump, even getting one on his college teammate Walter Clayton. It’s a great performance, but it’s hard to project anything like this happening from him going forward.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Daniss Jenkins (DET): Daniss Jenkins had 17 points (7-of-16 FGs), four rebounds, nine assists and three three-pointers in the Pistons’ 122-109 victory over the Pelicans on Wednesday.
item.description:
Daniss Jenkins had 17 points (7-of-16 FGs), four rebounds, nine assists and three three-pointers in the Pistons’ 122-109 victory over the Pelicans on Wednesday.

Jenkins has been excellent as he’s helped the Pistons to wins over the Spurs and Pelicans on back-to-back nights. The 25-year-old guard combined for 42 points, nine rebounds and 14 assists in the last two games. The Pistons resume NBA Cup play Friday against the Raptors at home.

Nick Shlain

item.title: [Recap] Kyrie Irving (DAL): Kyrie Irving had 17 points (7-of-15 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, three steals, and a three in the 116-94 win over the Mavericks.
item.description:
Kyrie Irving had 17 points (7-of-15 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, three steals, and a three in the 116-94 win over the Mavericks.

Another very standard Kyrie game where did everything necessary to get you the win. You’d wish for more points, but getting the six rebounds is a nice bump from what Kyrie has been averaging on the season. The Mavs next play the Clippers on Saturday.

item.description:
P.J. Washington had 21 points (7-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, a steal, three blocks, and five 3-pointers in win on Wednesday against Warriors.

P.J. Washington had his random game where he explodes and hits most of his shots. Before this game, he was averaging less than a steal and a block, so naturally he got a steal and three blocks in this one. He’s nothing more than a streamer and if you want some points, threes, and rebounds.

item.title: [Recap] Cooper Flagg (DAL): Cooper Flagg put up 33 points (11-of-15 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), five rebounds, nine assists, three steals, three 3-pointers, and five turnovers in win.
item.description:
Cooper Flagg put up 33 points (11-of-15 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), five rebounds, nine assists, three steals, three 3-pointers, and five turnovers in win.

The small buy low window has officially closed with this blowout performance against the Warriors. Now, it’s still the Warriors without Stephen Curry, so it’s not like the team has been an incredibly good team, but it’s good to see him get back on track. He will likely finish in the first-round range of most redraft leagues.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Injury] Al Horford (GSW): Al Horford (injury management) will not play against the Mavericks on Wednesday, but will play on Thursday against Grizzlies.
item.description:
Al Horford (injury management) will not play against the Mavericks on Wednesday, but will play on Thursday against Grizzlies.

Horford has not been what you would’ve hoped this season but that is to be expected with his age. On a low volume day, you could consider a stream of Horford as Draymond Green will be out, but the minutes won’t be very high and he’ll likely only be useful in deeper leagues.

item.title: Anfernee Simons (PHI): Anfernee Simons, VJ Edgecombe, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, LeBron James and Joel Embiid will start Wednesday’s game against the Magic.
item.description:
Anfernee Simons, VJ Edgecombe, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, LeBron James and Joel Embiid will start Wednesday’s game against the Magic.

Precious Achiuwa (ankle) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Suns.

item.title: [Recap] Brandon Miller (CHA): Brandon Miller notched 28 points (10-of-19 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Brandon Miller notched 28 points (10-of-19 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.

Fantasy managers have been waiting for Miller to snap out of his shooting slump for quite some time, and he may have done so on Tuesday. The Hornets wing shot over 50 percent from the field, and 28 points was the most he’s scored in a game since October 28 against the Pistons. Miller has been asked to create more looks for himself off the dribble, and it’s been a struggle. Miller is still shooting 35.9 percent from the field, so the buy-low window may not be closed just yet. Also, while he played 32 minutes, the Hornets shut Miller down at the end of regulation, leaving him to watch overtime from the bench.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Naz Reid (CHA): Naz Reid (nose) accounted for 23 points (8-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, four assists, two steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Naz Reid (nose) accounted for 23 points (8-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, four assists, two steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.

The line Reid recorded against the Lakers was in line with what many fantasy managers hoped to see from him consistently in Charlotte. Unfortunately, things haven’t worked out that way, and Tuesday’s overtime loss dropped the Hornets to 4-10. Making matters worse for Reid was an inadvertent elbow from Collin Sexton that he took to the nose late in overtime. He was subbed out and did not return. With Coby White and Brandon Miller shut down at the end of regulation, the Hornets lacked the options needed to potentially force a second overtime.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Coby White (CHA): Coby White finished Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers with 19 points (6-of-12 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, three steals and two three-pointers.
item.description:
Coby White finished Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers with 19 points (6-of-12 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, three steals and two three-pointers.

Although White has played in each of Charlotte’s last seven games, the team continues to limit his minutes. He logged 26 minutes on Tuesday and, along with Brandon Miller, did not play at all in overtime. The injuries and minutes restrictions the Hornets have dealt with have a lot to do with them being the worst fourth-quarter team in the NBA this season. Down the stretch on Tuesday, White and the other Hornets failed to do much offensively, with even inbounding the ball becoming an adventure. Charlotte doesn’t play again until Friday, which may be a good thing for White.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Kevon Looney (LAL): Kevon Looney finished Tuesday’s loss to the Hornets with four points (2-of-3 FGs) and seven rebounds.
item.description:
Kevon Looney finished Tuesday’s loss to the Hornets with four points (2-of-3 FGs) and seven rebounds.

With Walker Kessler (leg) out, the Lakers turned to Looney to start at center on Tuesday. While the veteran center grabbed seven rebounds, he played only 17 minutes, and his mobility was an issue. With Sandro Mamukelashvili (3/3/2/1) shooting 1-of-8 from the field, Lakers head coach JJ Redick eventually turned to two-way contract player Carson Cooper. While his numbers (3/4/2 in 18 minutes) won’t jump off the page, Cooper’s contributions as a rebounder and defender were one reason why the Lakers were able to rally. Kessler is expected to be available for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz, so Looney may find himself out of the rotation once again.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Luka Dončić (LAL): Luka Dončić tallied 36 points (13-of-34 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets.
item.description:
Luka Dončić tallied 36 points (13-of-34 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets.

Dončić didn’t have a great night shooting-wise, going 5-of-16 from three, but he still posted a complete stat line. The Lakers’ star has scored at least 32 points in 11 straight appearances, with the Lakers going 9-2 in those games. With Tuesday’s overtime win, the Lakers boast the best record in the Western Conference, something few expected at any point this season. Dončić has played like an MVP so far, whether the conversation is focused on the “actual” basketball or the fantasy basketball.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Quentin Grimes (LAL): Quentin Grimes amassed 47 points (16-of-24 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and 10 three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets.
item.description:
Quentin Grimes amassed 47 points (16-of-24 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and 10 three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets.

Grimes had the best game of his career on Tuesday, and the Lakers needed it, trailing by as much as 18 late in the third quarter before rallying to win in overtime. Grimes scored 21 points in the fourth quarter alone, outscoring the Hornets by four, and his three-pointer with 1.7 seconds left forced overtime. Austin Reaves (heel) is supposed to test his injured heel on Wednesday before that night’s game against the Jazz, so we should learn more about how much time he’ll miss. Grimes, the first Laker other than Reaves, Luka Dončić or LeBron James to record a 30-point game since Dalton Knecht did in March 2025, will start as long as Reaves is out, and he’s worth rostering until that changes.

item.description:
Jayson Tatum accumulated 32 points (11-of-18 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), seven rebounds, six assists and two steals over 30 minutes to lead the Celtics to a 131-94 blowout win over the Mavericks on Sunday.

Tatum put together a feast-worthy stat line just in time for Thanksgiving, exploding for 21 third-quarter points to extend Boston’s lead to 33 and effectively put the game out of reach before the final period. It marked the 10th time he has scored at least 15 points in a quarter, the most in Celtics history since the play-by-play era began in 1996-97, just ahead of franchise legend Paul Pierce. He’s delivered second-round fantasy value, averaging 26.8 points, 6.1 rebounds, 7.3 assists, 0.6 steals and 0.8 blocks through 12 games this season. The Celtics have won six consecutive games and will kick off a busy four-game week against the Magic before heading out west to face the Nuggets, Clippers and Warriors.

George Bissell

item.description:

Simply put, Dallas looked like a completely different offense without primary initiator Kyrie Irving at point guard as he sat out the second night of a back-to-back in this one. The 19-year-old phenom has cooled off a bit over the last week, but he’s still averaging 23.5 points, 6.7 rebounds, 6.2 assists, 1.9 steals and 0.8 blocks through 13 games as one of the most impactful all-around contributors in fantasy.
